correctness.rationale: Orthogonal Bergman monomial norms h_n=Gamma(n+1)Gamma(alpha+2)/Gamma(n+alpha+2) give C_r=c_r U_r+compact with c_r=r^{-(alpha+1)/2}. The exact identity U_p*U_q=U_b U_a* (a=p/gcd,b=q/gcd) produces infinitely repeated half-line or finite Jacobi paths whose adjacency essential spectrum is [-2,2]. Independently checked Chebyshev characteristic polynomials and path traces at lengths 2–10. Calkin mapping then yields [(c_p-c_q)^2,(c_p+c_q)^2]. Missing positive degrees force infinite cokernel if p,q>=2, while I-c_q U_q is invertible for p=1 via Neumann series. Nonzero gap implies closed range and lowest positive monomial degree shows constants are the entire kernel. Hardy c_p=c_q=1 gives [0,4] and nonclosed range; finite paths do not alone prove the infinite operator but the direct-sum argument does.
risks: No formal Lean or expert attestation; independent analytic reasoning and bounded symbolic tests do not certify every hidden assumption.
